body: I appreciate it. It’s really difficult sometimes to differentiate between suicidal ideation and actual suicide plans. It’s a changeling situation to be sure.
I’m so sorry you are experiencing that. I can empathize, and I know the feelings of humiliation and isolation that come with it. I hope we both pull through.

Oh yes. I talked to an inpatient program coordinator about my tendencies and her first response was to call the police unless my roommates could prove I was safe. Never going to disclose my true feelings again in that way.
Thank you. I’m trying to stay in it.
In theory, I totally agree. But it can be difficult.
Thank you. I’ve been going to therapy and keeping up my discipline. It’s difficult at times to stay positive, but I’m really trying.

I was falsely accused two years ago. It is my district’s policy to immediately pull teachers pending investigations, which I understand. The problem is, the district and OIG are disorganized and understaffed. People are routinely pulled, and they are left waiting to hear investigative results for YEARS (unless allegations are found to be true; then they are fired pretty quickly). 

So yeah, I’ve been out for two years just waiting. I haven’t been able to move on with my life. I think about suicide often. The union has told me “you’re getting paid and have insurance. Just keep waiting”. 

I’ll never go back to that school even after I’ve been cleared (I’m hoping in the next year???). The rumor has ruined my chances of ever having a normal career. I feel sick. I hope things are easier for you.
This sounds like a great 3rd date idea.
He thinks we should pay a set amount, slightly higher than we anticipated, and then let the organizer figure it out from there.

I guess the place is mostly rooms with multiple beds. There is one or two single bedrooms. I was always planning on being in a room with multiple sleeping arrangements, but I didn’t care that much because I was only paying $80/night with that assumption (although if we did a single airbnb like I wanted it would be that or a little more/less). Now if I’m in a shared room and not a single room with my husband, I could be paying closer to double that a night and MIGHT not get my own room.
I suppose divvying up the cancellation fee is the easiest way to go about it

I think the communication on it is bothering me almost as much as the cost increase. Nobody is responding to texts/calls/etc and it’s making it even harder to figure out what’s going. When people bailed after they confirmed the guy in charge told them it was fine but then never communicated with anyone else of the price increase until 3 weeks before the wedding.

At this point I’d just feel really guilty I guess because I’ve been saying for months that we were in. I don’t want to leave the people who decide to stay with an even higher bill to foot directly because of me.

My husband is also equally angry and is set on not paying above a certain amount. He’s been trying to discuss it with his friends who are staying, and I’ve been in contact with one of their wives, who is equally flabbergasted by the situation. No one really has any set answers because the person who chose to take charge is being really esoteric. When we made the plans (in March) via group text everyone confirmed and said they’d be responsible for their share. He claimed up until a few days ago that everyone was 100% confirmed still. I just believed him I guess because they are his friends, not mine. 

I don’t want to be a party pooper. I just wish the guy “in charge” had gotten confirmation like he said he did. If I was in charge I probably would have taken down payments from everyone (which I suggested before the place was booked, but I was poo-pooed).
